label: end-of-episode clock: last ~10 trials, delay steps (D1/D2), silent at GO
explanation: A time-in-episode unit. It never fires before episode trial ~60, starts firing weakly around trials 70-89, and is concentrated in trials 90-99 (92% of activation mass, rate 42%). Within those trials it fires on the D1 and D2 delay steps and is almost silent at GO (0.7% of mass). It is strongly tied to the low value-head output that comes with the approaching episode end: 94% of mass falls in the lowest value bin. Magnitude rises steadily with trial index toward the episode end, as the per-window ramps show. Inside the late-episode D2 steps it fires preferentially when the reached state is S1 (precision 0.92 for late D2 & state==S1). At D1 it is larger after an unrewarded trial, but that clause is imprecise. Adding these state/reward clauses gained only about 1 point of F1, so I recorded the simple time x phase predicate. Precision is limited (about 0.61) because not every late delay step is active, and recall misses the weaker activations from trials 80-89. Uses no future variables: ep_trial is not an explicit input but the agent can track elapsed time internally.
